newsitem.title: USA: Rating agencies caution issuers on investments.
newsitem.headline: Rating agencies caution issuers on investments.

text.p: Officials from Standard & Poor's Corp. and Moody's Investors Service said Friday that municipal bond issuers should exercise caution with the investments they make.
Joe O'Keefe, a director at Standard & Poor's, said issuers should demand complete and timely disclosure of investment risk.
"They should be asking questions about disclosure," he said. "They should be looking at the financial statements from their advisers."

The comments came in the wake of news that pooled school investment funds in Illinois and Michigan had invested in commercial paper of a troubled consumer finance company that defaulted last week on its short-term lending agreements.
"We would expect all the paper in the fund to have ratings and be investment grade," said Linda Lipnick, a vice president and manager of the north central region at Moody's.
Mercury Finance Co had enjoyed investment grade ratings from Standard & Poor's and Duff & Phelps prior to news of its financial troubles.

The Lake Forest, Ill.-based consumer finance company, last week restated its last four year's earnings lower by a total of about $90 million after discovering accounting discrepancies. The company later said it was in default on its short-term lending agreements.
The company has also been served with a Federal Bureau of Investigation search warrant seeking financial documents.
